extracted.intended_audience: regulated industries, agency compliance officers, and legal practitioners (e.g., whalers, rubber-tire manufacturers, telephone carriers, exchanges, shippers, and import/export/customs officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of formal federal regulations, orders, and procedural requirements governing conduct (whaling, animal import controls, trade practices, records retention, securities filings, hearings, and agricultural marketing). Includes substantive prohibitions, definitional criteria, exceptions, filing timelines, and record-keeping/destruction standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Whaling Convention and Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 1: The provisions of the Convention for the Regulation of Whaling, The Whaling Treaty Act, and these regulations apply to all nationals, vessels, and boats of the United States in all the waters of the world, and to all persons, vessels, and boats in the United States, its territories and possessions, including the territorial waters thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species included as baleens or whalebone whales
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 2: Baleens or whalebone whales included within the terms of the Convention and the Act include, among others, enumerated species under headings RIGHT WHALES, GRAY WHALES, BLUE WHALES, FIN WHALES, HUMPBACK WHALES, LEAST RORQUALS, and specific named varieties (e.g., Atlantic right whale, Bowhead, California gray, Blue whale, Finback, Humpback, Minke's whale, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists many species by common names and synonyms; use the list for identification of regulated species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of calves/immature whales by length
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 3: Calves or suckling (immature) whales are defined by length measured from snout tip to tail notch; minimum lengths: Blue whales 60 feet, Fin (pin) whales 50 feet, Humpback whales 35 feet, Sei whales 40 feet, Least rorquals 18 feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length thresholds determine whether an animal is a calf/immature for protection under prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted acts for baleen/whalebone whales (general allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 4: The hunting, taking, capturing, killing, possession, sale, purchase, shipment, transportation, carriage, import, or export of any baleen or whalebone whale, or possession, sale, purchase, shipment, transportation, carriage, import, or export of the products thereof, except as provided in the following article, shall be deemed compatible with the terms of said Convention and permitted by these Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art. 4 establishes general permissibility subject to Art. 5 exceptions; consult Art. 5 for prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited taking/commerce in right and gray whales and calves
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 5: The hunting, taking, capturing, killing, possession, sale, purchase, shipment, transportation, carriage, import, or export of any right or gray whale, or of any calf, suckling, or immature whale, or of any female whale accompanied by any calf, suckling, or immature whale, or the possession, sale, purchase, shipment, transportation, carriage, import, or export of the products thereof, shall be deemed incompatible with the terms of the Convention and prohibited by these regulations except as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two explicit exceptions are provided (scientific permits and native/Eskimo subsistence whaling under strict conditions). Collectors/customs must require evidence of authorizations on import/export.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific-permit exception for prohibited whales
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 5(a): Exception — for scientific purposes under a special permit issued by the Secretary of Commerce. For each such importation or exportation of any such whale or the product (including oil, meat, bone, meal, fertilizer), competent evidence that the Secretary of Commerce has authorized such importation or exportation must be presented to the Collector of Customs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competent evidence must be presented at port of importation/exportation; applies to prohibited species/products when authorized for science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native/Eskimo subsistence exception and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 5(b): Exception — natives or Eskimos engaged in whaling who use only canoes or native craft propelled by oars or sails, do not carry firearms, are not employed by non-natives, and are not under contract to deliver products to third parties. Collector of Customs in Alaska may require satisfactory evidence; other collectors shall require presentation of satisfactory evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importers/exporters claiming this exception must provide satisfactory evidence at port; conditions are strictly enumerated (craft type, no firearms, no employment by outsiders, no delivery contracts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-application to dolphins/porpoises and state law savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 6: Nothing in these regulations shall be construed as applying to dolphins or porpoises; nor shall anything permit acts contrary to laws and regulations of any State or Territory giving further protection to whales when such laws are not inconsistent with the Convention or The Whaling Treaty Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal regs do not cover dolphins/porpoises and do not preempt state laws that offer greater protection consistent with the Convention/Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing requirements for proposed marketing agreement/order (onions, CO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Docket No. A-350-35 Notice: Under the Agricultural Adjustment Act and General Regulations, notice of hearing is required for a proposed marketing agreement/order regulating handling of onions in Colorado; hearing times/places provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing purpose: receive evidence on general economic conditions necessitating regulation, specific provisions the agreement/order should contain, and whether to include shipment limitations by period pro ration; copies of proposed documents available from Hearing Clerk; emergency finding can shorten notice period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency declaration shortens notice period
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice: It is declared that an emergency exists in handling of onions requiring a shorter period of notice than fifteen (15) days; determined that the period of notice given is reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows abbreviated notice for hearings where emergency is declared; agencies must state basis and declare reasonableness of shorter notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order terminating amended license — non-waiver and reservation clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Order Terminating the Amended License for Shippers of Oranges and Grapefruit: Termination does not (a) affect, waive, or terminate any right, duty, or obligation which has arisen or may arise in connection with the license; (b) release or forgive any violation of the license occurring prior to termination; (c) affect or impair any rights or remedies of the Secretary of Agriculture or any other person with respect to any violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination preserves pre-existing rights, obligations, remedies, and enforcement for prior violations despite termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau of Animal Industry — country listings for disease import controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment 5 to B.A.I. Order 353: The list of countries subject to the order to prevent introduction of rinderpest and foot-and-mouth disease is amended by restoring 'Great Britain' (disease present) and striking 'Hungary' (determined free). These determinations are notified to the Secretary of the Treasury; prior amendment revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Country lists for import controls are adjusted based on disease determinations; effective dates and prior amendments may be revoked; agencies must notify Treasury.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC: Records exempted from Telephone Division Order No. 14 (destruction of records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission Order No. 17 exempts from Telephone Division Order No. 14 a wide range of records described in subsections of paragraph 20 (e.g., 1(d) subscribers' end pay station ledgers and equivalents; 5(f) canceled capital stock certificates; 6(f) canceled bonds and paid interest coupons; 10(d) record of index of bills; 16 retired securities (canceled stock certificates, bonds, notes, etc.); 18(e)-(g) fire reports, minor loss reports, watchmen's reports; 31(f) advice of deposits when info shown elsewhere; 41(b),(c),(d),(e),(g) various bill stubs, copies, statements of collections, coin box records, statements of amounts collected from employees; 71(m),(o) copies of shipping instructions and records used for checking/tracing material; and numerous other categories such as motor vehicle records not used for charges, temporary removal receipts, employee delivery receipts, registered mail receipts, surrendered passes, lunch ticket records, mileage records, adding-machine lists, records of forms, fire drill records, postage stamp records, transmittal lists, duplicate records, stenographers' notebook records, extra copies of letters, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed categories may be destroyed or exempted from prior retention requirements provided carriers still comply with Telephone Division Orders Nos. 6-A and 6-B regarding retention of original records containing data used in compiling required reports. Duplicates may be destroyed if originals or other copies retain all information.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC guidance on duplicate records and temporary receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission allows destruction of duplicate accounts, records and memoranda if all information is contained on originals/other retained copies and if duplicates are not specifically provided for; receipts for records/papers temporarily removed are exempt when items returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep originals or authorized copies; duplicates and temporary receipts may be destroyed only when originals retained as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTC Trade Practice Rules — Group I (illegal/unfair methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promulgated rules designed to foster fair competition; Group I rules describe unfair methods of competition deemed illegal under statutes/case law and enforceable by the Commission. Violations will prompt proceedings to prevent such practices in interstate commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group I rules are mandatory (unfair/illegal); Group II are industry-desirable practices but not per se illegal unless they have unfair-competition effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1(a): Prohibited discriminatory price differentials, rebates, discounts, credits, allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an unfair trade practice for any member to grant or allow any price differentials, rebates, refunds, discounts, credits, or other allowances which effectuate price discrimination between purchasers of like grade/quality where purchases are in commerce and the effect may substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly or injure competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) sales within U.S. jurisdiction; (2) differentials that make due allowance for cost differences of manufacture/sale/delivery; (3) bona fide customer selection; (4) price changes responding to changing market conditions (perishable goods, obsolescence, distress sales, discontinuance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1(b): Prohibited brokerages and commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfair to pay or receive anything of value as commission, brokerage, or analogous compensation except for services rendered in connection with sale/purchase, and except where intermediary is acting in fact for a party other than the payer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents concealed or improper brokerage that may mask anti-competitive arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1(c): Prohibited advertising or promotional allowances lacking proportional equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfair to pay or contract for advertising or promotion allowances or other things of value to a customer as compensation for services/facilities furnished in connection with processing/handling/sale unless such payment is available on proportionally equal terms to all competing customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires non-discriminatory availability of promotional allowances to competing customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1(d): Prohibited discriminatory services or facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfair to discriminate in favor of one purchaser over others by furnishing or contracting to furnish services or facilities connected with processing/handling/sale on terms not accorded proportionally to all purchasers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to services/facilities that affect competitive parity among purchasers/resellers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1(e): Illegal price discrimination under Clayton Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfair to discriminate in price contrary to Section 2 of the Clayton Act (as amended) or to give or receive a discrimination prohibited by that section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References statutory prohibition; carriers must comply with amended Clayton Act provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 2: Prohibition on defamation/false disparagement of competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an unfair trade practice to defame competitors by falsely imputing dishonorable conduct, inability to perform, questionable credit standing, or by false disparagement of grade/quality/manufacture or business methods with tendency to mislead purchasers/public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers false statements intended to mislead consumers or trade partners about competitors or their products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3: Selling below cost with intent to injure competitors (predatory pricing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selling goods below seller's cost, with intent and effect of injuring a competitor and where effect may substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly is an unfair trade practice; all elements recognized by good accounting practice are to be included in determining cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost determination must follow sound accounting practice; intent and effect tests apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4: Prohibition of false, untrue or deceptive statements/advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Making or permitting false, untrue or deceptive statements, representations, guarantees, warranties, or adjustment policies about grade, quality, quantity, use, character, origin, life/service of tires/tubes, or any other material aspect, with tendency to mislead purchasers/public, is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers advertising, labeling, and other communications; material misrepresentations actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5: Prohibition on false or deceptive marking/branding
rubrics_metrics.description: False or deceptive marking or branding of industry products for purpose or effect of misleading purchasers about grade, quality, quantity, size, material, origin, manufacture, or distribution is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires truthful marking/branding of tires and related goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6: Misrepresenting authorization/character of business
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfair to hold oneself out as 'an authorized dealer' when not such, or to misrepresent character of one's business in ways tending to mislead purchasers/public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects consumers and trade partners from false dealer-authority claims and business mischaracterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7: Misrepresentation of handling 'all standard makes'
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfair to represent that one handles 'all standard makes' of tires/tubes when not true, with tendency to mislead purchasers/public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires accuracy in claims about range of products stocked or handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8: Falsely representing 'change over' or used tires as new
rubrics_metrics.description: Falsely representing 'change over' tires or tubes as new or unused when they are not is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers representations about condition of tires offered for sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 9: Making invoices or sale tickets false in whole or part
rubrics_metrics.description: Withholding from or inserting in invoice or sale ticket statements that make it a false record of the transaction, with purpose or effect of misleading purchasers/public, is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounting/documentation integrity required; falsified sales records prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10(a): Passing off used/rebuilt/recapped/retreaded/repaired tires as new
rubrics_metrics.description: Passing off, selling, or offering used, rebuilt, recapped, retreaded, or repaired tires as new or unused is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition against misrepresenting secondhand or reconditioned tires as new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10(b): Branding/labeling requirements for used/rebuilt tires
rubrics_metrics.description: Sale of used/rebuilt/recapped/retreaded/repaired tires that have been dressed to simulate new must be durably and conspicuously branded or molded with words like 'Secondhand', 'Used tire—rebuilt', 'Used tire—recapped', 'Used tire—retreaded', or 'Used tire—repaired', or otherwise fully and truthfully disclosed to purchasers and users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Durable, conspicuous branding is required to prevent deception; full disclosure to purchasers and users is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11: Misrepresentation of quality or grade
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct or indirect misrepresentation of tires as being of a higher quality/grade than they are, or misrepresenting line/grade ranking, with tendency to mislead purchasers/public, is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires truthful statements about quality/grade classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 12: Misleading illustrations in advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use in advertisements of illustrations or depictions of tires/tubes different in brand, style, size, or higher grade than the products to which the representations apply, with tendency to mislead purchasers/public, is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations must truthfully depict the specific products being advertised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13: Limited-offer disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements or representations of tires or prices applicable only to limited sizes/lines/grades/styles/brands must truthfully and unequivocally disclose such limitations; failure to do so is an unfair trade practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory clear disclosure of limitations on advertised offers/prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group II: Industry-condemned but not per se illegal practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Group II practices are considered unethical, uneconomical, or desirable to avoid by the industry; compliance depends on industry cooperation. Such practices are received by the Commission where conforming to specifics and not violative of law, but may be prosecuted if used to become unfair methods of competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group II rules are aspirational/advisory unless they take on anti-competitive effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule A (Group II): Differentiation between wholesale and retail transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Condemned: Failure to correctly differentiate between wholesale and retail transactions in the same establishment where result may create confusion and deception as to transaction character in purchasers' minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retailers/wholesalers must clearly identify transaction type to avoid deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule B (Group II): Marking number of plies on pneumatic tires
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry judgment that manufacturers should mark or brand pneumatic automobile tires with words/figures/phrases molded in/on each side wall (or otherwise permanently affixed) to indicate unequivocally, conspicuously, and truthfully the number of plies in tire construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for public safety and to protect purchasers from deception; marks should be permanent and conspicuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC Rule CB4: Keeping applications for exemption up-to-date (amendments and supplements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every exchange applying for or granted exemption from registration as a national securities exchange shall keep its application up-to-date: (a) Amendments — file promptly after discovery of any inaccuracy; (b) Current supplements — file promptly after any change rendering information inaccurate, with specified exceptions for Exhibits C, D, E and certain items; (c) Periodic supplements — quarterly/monthly/annual supplements for detailed information (e.g., Exhibits C, D, E quarterly; Exhibit I semimonthly reporting option; annual balance sheet/income statements for exchange and affiliates); (d) All amendments/supplements filed in triplicate, dated and numbered, at least one signed and attested, conforming to Rule A2 and Form 9-A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where no current supplements needed are enumerated (published weekly info, semimonthly filings for Exhibit I, and certain Exhibits B/J); exchanges must also send three copies of notices/reports/circulars when made available to members.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC: Filing formalities for amendments and supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every amendment or supplement shall be filed in triplicate, at least one copy signed and attested in the same manner as the original registration or application, conforming to Rule A2 and Form 9-A. Amendments/supplements must be dated and numbered in order of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/format requirements are mandatory; one amendment may include many changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC orders directing hearings — grounds and procedural powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders set hearings when Commission deems necessary for protection of investors, e.g., application to withdraw listing or belief that registration statement contains untrue statements/omissions. Hearings appointed with time/place; an officer is designated to administer oaths, subpoena witnesses, compel attendance, take evidence, require production of books/papers/records, close hearings, and report to the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officers have full evidentiary and procedural authority; general notice of hearings is required so interested persons may be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC orders fixing time/place for hearings under Securities Act Section 8(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reasonable grounds exist to believe registration statements include untrue statements of material facts or omit material facts, the Commission orders a hearing under Section 8(d) with specified date, time, place, and designated officer to take evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such orders are issued to investigate material misstatements/omissions and to protect investors; officers report findings to Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC Order for continuance — Rule VI practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission may grant continuances of hearings upon proper request pursuant to Rule VI of the Commission's Rules of Practice; the order will set a new date/time/place and preserve the same trial examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuances are discretionary but may be granted to accommodate parties/agency requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-keeping/retention caveat (FCC telephone carriers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission's exemptions do not relieve telephone carriers from compliance with Telephone Division Orders Nos. 6-A and 6-B relating to retention of original records containing the data used in compiling responses to those orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where categories are exempted from general destruction rules, original records containing required data must be retained as specified by other orders.
